sents.text: So what do you need?
For the next lesson, just a Google account and a web browser.
Soon, a free GitHub account.
And for the laptop lessons, any laptop with eight gigabytes of memory will do, and sixteen is comfortable.
No laptop?
No problem.
The first courses run entirely in your browser, even on a tablet.
Every lab in this series tells you which step of the workbench it uses.
Labs start on a small sample of data, then scale up, so you see for yourself why tools change with size.
And labs never hand you the full code.
Instead, they prompt you one step at a time: what to install, what to load, what to try next.
You build it, so you understand it.
One more thing, and it's the same lesson as last time.
Simpler wins.
Start in Colab.
Move to your laptop when you want to work offline.
And climb to the bigger steps only when your data truly needs them.
Don't build a data centre to analyse a spreadsheet.
Let's recap.
Your workbench is one setup for every course and every job.
It lives online and offline, and all your work sits in one GitHub repository called workbench.
It grows in five steps as your data grows, and every step mirrors the tools real companies use.
